owner_proof_sketch: Read the raw game, construction fields and exact sampler projection laws.
Read the raw game and sampler projection laws; the tail is the same uniform.
Read the core's public vectors, pass to acceptance expectations, and sum out the unused uniform vectors using the existing exact uniform expectation law.
Read the public vectors and use the uniform expectation law to marginalize the unused draw inside acceptance probability.
Couple the two games with the same draws and coins. Correctness and the packing readers show agreement off err=true; use the existing agree-off-bad bound.
Couple the same draws and uniform output. The public seeds agree when err=false; apply the existing agree-off-bad bound.
Apply the existing `LWE.encodeChallenge_injective` with the LWE family's public modulus-width field.
Split the nested pairs, recover hop/index/bucket/draw/tail coordinates, and use modular vector injectivity on each uniform-vector list entry.

Use the existing pair/list/vector length equations, the exact draw layout, the published numeric bounds, κOf(L)≤L and PolyExpr.eval_mono; the factor4096 covers all separators in the deliberately generous cubic majorant.

For each scheduled dimension, average over every nonchallenge value and fix a maximizing advice tuple. Reindex at ℓ(κ), transport the canonical challenge by its explicit equivalence, and use the shared realiser verdict/coin readers. Uniform coin prefixes recover A's coins; the resulting gap is bounded by the LPN advantage.
Read the canonical challenge pair through prgEnc_eq and challengeStr_eq, then apply the primitive's index-code injectivity and List.ofFn injectivity.
Split the nested pairs, apply the bucket-code and canonical matrix-code injectivity readers at the public prime's residue width, then use record extensionality.

Read the nested pair lengths and canonical matrix lengths. Bound buckets and the LPN matrix by idxBound, and the repeated uniform vectors by the public seed bound with residue width kappa+1. Apply kappaOfN_le and polynomial evaluation monotonicity, then absorb all constant and linear factors into the stated cubic majorant.

At each Boolean parameter, average over bucket maps, public matrices and uniform public vectors, and fix advice whose absolute acceptance gap dominates the average. At image parameters use kappaOfN_n and the preprocessing readers to identify the canonical Boolean challenge with the two chain endpoints. Transport the realiser's typed coins through RealizesOn's published readers and remove the unused coin suffix using the existing prefix sampling lemma. Choose arbitrary inhabited advice off the image and assemble the family.

Choose the largest gap in the real-tail chain, hardwire its other draws in LPN advice at every inverse-indexed dimension, and apply the every-realiser hop lemma. Use the PRG hop on the all-uniform public vectors, then the existing hybrid inequality.

Bound H0-H1 and H2-H3 by the error event. Connect H1 to H2 by the real-tail LPN chain, the PRG hop, and the reversed uniform-tail LPN chain. At each κ choose the largest of the 2κ LPN gaps and hardwire the remaining draws. The shared realiser readers identify every realiser's verdict, and the existing hybrid inequalities sum the gaps. At κ=0 only the PRG hop and the explicit error slack remain.

Instantiate the advice from prop41 and the realisers from Realizable. Reindex negligible LPN and PRG advantages along ℓ≥κ and n≥κ. Multiply by the polynomial 2κ, add the Claim 4.2 slack, and use the shared negligibility closure lemmas.

Reindex the LPN term by κ^E and PRG term by κ^(E*D). Use the shared polynomial-factor and constant-factor closure lemmas at an intermediate exponent below the common minimum. Claim 4.2 controls the error term by 2^(-κ). Two applications of sum closure yield half the minimum, then prop41 gives domination of the advantage.
Read the two shared SubexpHard witnesses, use jls_subexpSmall, and observe that its positive exponent depends only on the assumption exponents and P.
Combine raw security, the G4 correctness/degree theorem, and Claim 4.1.
Combine jls_subexpSecure, G4 correctness/degree, and Claim 4.1.
Choose E=max 1 E0, build Params from the given G and representation, and apply theorem41 with the supplied family assumption and realisability.
Choose the same sufficiently large schedule exponent and apply theorem41_subexp to the supplied family hardness and realisability.

For each reduction, specialize its single preprocessing map at π. Apply exists_realizesOn_of_preTarget with the inverse parameter map, polynomial var, the explicit advice encoding and length bound. Match the named reduction by its reader.
Specialize the target at pp=π κ and read the raw construction's encodings.
Read the draw and core witnesses, restrict public parameters to π κ, and join them with SamplesEfficiently.intro, using the raw field readers.
Restrict the universal pp/index parameter to the supplied schedule. Read the unchanged core and encoding witnesses and join the two shared contract halves.
Read the universal schedule-parametrized witness and specialize its equivalence and equations at π. Retain the same uniform sampler, polynomial and map.
Use G4 as the polynomial witness, the target's term-list equations, its degree theorem, and exact sampled-seed correctness.
Targets provide realisability and the primitive's honest efficiency. Apply the raw theorem, transport its properties through jlsSPRG_toRaw, and use T2 for efficient polynomial generation.
Choose E=max 1 E0, specialize the targets to those parameters, and apply theorem41_of_targets to the given Boolean PRG and construction-family assumption.
Choose a sufficiently large E, use the raw subexponential theorem and T2, then assemble the primitive from the specialized target witnesses.
